title: The Black Prince of Norway and a jazz chapter
summary: For eleven months he was a big man in Norway, nicknamed the Black Prince, taught audiences to clap and swing, and organised a jazz society with British trumpeter Roland Greenberg.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: Until one day, they said you got to leave man, because this is it. I went to Fenmark -- it's way up there -- lapland is there. You couldn't get no boats coming out --
You couldn't get any boats out?
No, you couldn't get any ships -- and they said, you go to Fenmark and stay there. Because I was
*Mr. Butler later recalled this ship to be the Bismarck.
Prinz-- called the Swart), the Black Prince in Norway, I was the Black Prince. Cause I had taught them how to clap their hands and swing and everything else, man.

For eleven months I was a big man there. And in the meantime, while we was there, there was a little fellow who played trumpet, he come from England, his name was Roland Greenberg. Played beautiful trumpet.
And we organized a jazz -- jazz chapter in-- That's when Jazz started to catch over in Norway.
